svg.title: The minimum squared distance is feasible and globally least
svg.desc: For A zero,five quarters and P t,t squared with zero at most t at most two, squared distance D equals t to the fourth minus three halves t squared plus twenty-five sixteenths. Completing the square gives t squared minus three quarters squared, plus one. Therefore D is at least one, attained at t square root three over two in the allowed interval. The closest point is square root three over two,three quarters and its distance is one. Both endpoints are included; their squared distances twenty-five sixteenths and one hundred eighty-five sixteenths are larger.
